event_title: Dangerous Docs 2026: States of Emergency with Filmmakers
film_description: This evocative program of docu-shorts delves into catastrophe, not as a spectacle, but as a lived experience. It charts the emotional and physical aftermath of a world in constant upheaval, offering a powerful look at resilience in the face of crisis.
event_description: Experience 'Dangerous Docs 2026: States of Emergency,' a compelling program of documentary shorts examining the profound impact of global upheaval. The evening begins with plaza seating at 7:00 PM, followed by the film screenings starting at 8:15 PM. Conclude the night with an insightful Q&A session featuring the filmmakers at 9:45 PM.

event_title: Wendigo with Larry Fessenden (Director)
film_description: A family from the city decide to spend a weekend away at a friend's country farmhouse. But a fluke accident sets off a chain of events that alters their lives forever and conjures up the ferocious spirit of the Wendigo.
event_description: This special 25th-anniversary screening of Larry Fessenden's influential 2001 film, 'Wendigo,' about a family's encounter with vengeful forces in the wintry Catskills, will be followed by a Q&A with the director himself. The event is part of the 'Scary Movies XIV' festival and features a new 4K restoration.

event_title: Blind Fury with Adam Howard (Producer/Artist)
film_description: A blind Vietnam vet, trained as a swordfighter, comes to America and helps to rescue the son of a fellow soldier.
event_description: This screening of Blind Fury will be introduced by producer and artist Adam Howard. The film stars Rutger Hauer as Nick Parker, a visually impaired veteran drawn into conflict with a crime syndicate. Hauer's performance anchors this action-packed, comedic cult classic, celebrated for its unique blend of genres.

event_title: Goody Goody with Raymond Creamer (Director)
film_description: Lulled into a necessary sense of comfort during a long home birth process, expecting parents and their midwife begin to realize that something may be horribly wrong. As labor complications ensue, a blizzard rages outside trapping the family in their home – sitting ducks for whatever sinister presence might be in there with them.
event_description: The New York Premiere of "Goody Goody" will be screened as part of the Scary Movies XIV festival. The screening on Friday, August 14, will be followed by a Q&A session with director Raymond Creamer. Another screening is scheduled for Monday, August 17.

event_title: Coyote vs. Acme with Will Forte, Lana Condor
film_description: After Acme products fail him one too many times in his dogged pursuit of the Roadrunner, Wile E. Coyote decides to hire a billboard lawyer to sue the Acme Corporation.
event_description: This is a special advance screening of "Coyote vs. Acme" followed by an in-person Q&A session with cast members Will Forte and Lana Condor. The film runs for 103 minutes and is presented in DCP format.

event_title: Bodyhackers with Carlos Conceição (Director)
film_description: A story about people who reinvent their ideals of perfection to incorporate a sensual attraction to surgically transformed bodies.
event_description: This event features a North American Premiere screening of Carlos Conceição's film, Bodyhackers. Following the film, there will be a Q&A session with director Carlos Conceição. The film is presented as part of the Scary Movies XIV festival.

event_title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three with Bruce Goldstein (Film Forum Repertory Artistic Director)
film_title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
film_description: In New York, armed men hijack a subway car and demand a ransom for the passengers while the authorities question about the method of their escape.
event_presenters: Bruce Goldstein (Film Forum Repertory Artistic Director)
event_description: This special screening of "The Taking of Pelham One Two Three" will be preceded by an illustrated presentation given by Bruce Goldstein, Film Forum Repertory Artistic Director. The presentation will delve into other subway movies and highlight the precise details of PELHAM, offering insights into its context and historical significance.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Bruce Goldstein (Film Forum Repertory Artistic Director)

event_title: Family Movie with Kevin Bacon (Co-Director/Actor), Kyra Sedgwick (Co-Director/Actor), Travis Bacon (Actor)
film_description: The Smiths have gathered once again on their quaint family farm to make the latest in a string of low-budget horror movies. No, the movies aren't particularly "successful." Some might even call them "bad." But at least the family is together, and that's what matters to Jack and Ellen. Their adult children, on the other hand - Trent and Ula - are working up the courage to leave this particular family tradition behind. Simmering family dysfunction turns to pure chaos when a real dead body shows up on set. Can they come together to keep the movie on track, or will this be the Smith family's final act?
event_presenters: Kevin Bacon (Co-Director/Actor), Kyra Sedgwick (Co-Director/Actor), Travis Bacon (Actor)
event_description: The New York premiere of "Family Movie," co-directed and starring Kevin Bacon and Kyra Sedgwick, will include a screening followed by a Q&A session. Kevin Bacon, Kyra Sedgwick, and Travis Bacon will be in attendance to discuss the film.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Kevin Bacon (Co-Director/Actor), Kyra Sedgwick (Co-Director/Actor), Travis Bacon (Actor)

event_title: Sholay with Siddhant Adlakha (Film Critic)
film_description: After his family is slain by notorious bandit Gabbar Singh, former Inspector Thakur Baldev Singh enlists low-level outlaws Jai and Veeru to capture Gabbar and seek revenge.
event_description: Experience Ramesh Sippy's ambitious 1975 Bollywood classic, "Sholay," a 'curry Western' that was India's box-office champion for two decades. This screening presents the film with its astonishing original ending, previously censored and now restored by Film Heritage Foundation. The event on Wednesday, August 19th, will include an introduction by film critic Siddhant Adlakha.

event_title: Boyhood with Patricia Arquette (Star), Ethan Hawke (Star)
film_description: The film tells a story of a divorced couple trying to raise their young son. The story follows the boy for twelve years, from first grade at age 6 through 12th grade at age 17-18, and examines his relationship with his parents as he grows.
event_description: A special 12th anniversary screening of Richard Linklater's Boyhood, featuring a Q&A session with stars Patricia Arquette and Ethan Hawke after the 6:15 PM show, and an extended introduction by the stars at the 8:40 PM show. The film, shot over 12 years with the same cast, offers a unique portrayal of childhood and growing up.

event_title: Paper Trails, Chain Reactions with Nora Rodriguez (Filmmaker), Jodie Mack (Filmmaker), Kathryn Roake (Filmmaker), Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)
film_description: A curated collection of tactile animated films created on paper, emphasizing the constraints and texture of the page. These films reveal the residue of actions and cycles, where mysterious scenarios and personal histories are intertwined.
event_presenters: Nora Rodriguez (Filmmaker), Jodie Mack (Filmmaker), Kathryn Roake (Filmmaker), Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)
event_description: This event features a collection of tactile animated films curated by Lilli Carré, exploring animations crafted on paper that highlight the process and texture of the medium. The screening will be followed by a conversation with filmmakers Nora Rodriguez, Jodie Mack, Kathryn Roake, and guest-curator Lilli Carré. Prior to the film, there will be live music by Blk.wav featuring Frae-Frae & Shelley Nicole and food from La Cevicheria available starting at 6:30pm.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Nora Rodriguez (Filmmaker), Jodie Mack (Filmmaker), Kathryn Roake (Filmmaker), Kate Renshaw-Lewis (Filmmaker), Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)

event_title: The Threshing with Sean Mannion (Director)
film_description: The Threshing follows a young couple as they enter the world of regenerative farming. When they first arrive they revel in the bucolic bliss of their new mountainside home, but soon fall into the farm’s more sinister practices, descending from ritualistic animal slaughter to self-mutilation and cannibalism.
event_description: This North American Premiere of Sean Mannion's 'The Threshing' is the Closing Night film for Scary Movies XIV. The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with director Sean Mannion. Audiences have the option to purchase a film-only ticket or a ticket that includes access to a post-screening party. The event is part of the Scary Movies XIV festival, sponsored by Mubi.

event_title: Paper Trails, Chain Reactions with Nora Rodriguez, Jodie Mack, Kathryn Roake, Kate Renshaw-Lewis, Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)
film_description: This collection features tactile animated films created on paper, utilizing the constraints and texture of the page. The films explore how residue of actions and cycles reverberate, fusing mysterious scenarios with personal histories. Guest curated by Lilli Carré, the program delves into the unique aesthetic and narrative possibilities of paper-based animation.
event_presenters: Nora Rodriguez, Jodie Mack, Kathryn Roake, Kate Renshaw-Lewis, Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)
event_description: Experience 'Paper Trails, Chain Reactions,' a curated collection of tactile animated films created on paper. The evening will include a performance by Blk.wav featuring Frae-Frae & Shelley Nicole at 7:00 PM, followed by the film program at 8:00 PM. A post-screening conversation will be held with Nora Rodriguez, Jodie Mack, Kathryn Roake, Kate Renshaw-Lewis, and guest-curator Lilli Carré. Food from La Cevicheria will be available starting at 6:30 PM.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Nora Rodriguez, Jodie Mack, Kathryn Roake, Kate Renshaw-Lewis, Lilli Carré (Guest Curator)

event_title: 54: The Director's Cut with Mark Christopher (Director)
film_description: New York City, 1979: working class Jersey City teenager Shane becomes infatuated with Studio 54, a lavish Manhattan nightclub known for decadence. The film was originally heavily re-shot ahead of its theatrical release in 1998, before being re-assembled in a long-awaited director's cut in 2015, with over forty minutes of different footage used.
event_description: Experience the director's cut of '54,' followed by a Q&A session with director Mark Christopher. The film is an essential ode to old New York, anchored by an impressive performance from Ryan Phillippe and a bombastic, period-appropriate soundtrack.

event_title: Trees Lounge with Steve Buscemi (Director/Star)
film_description: Tommy has lost his job, his love and his life. He lives in a small apartment above the Trees Lounge, a bar which he frequents along with a few other regulars without lives. He gets a job driving an ice cream truck and ends up getting involved with the seventeen-year-old niece of his ex-girlfriend. This gets him into serious trouble with her father.
event_description: A special screening of "Trees Lounge" followed by a Q&A session with director and star Steve Buscemi. This event features a new 4K restoration by IndieCollect, scanned from the original 35mm color negative in collaboration with Buscemi and DP Lisa Rinzler. Limited benefit tickets are also available, including a pre-screening reception hosted by Steve Buscemi via IndieCollect.

event_title: Paper Flowers Q&A
film_description: Based on a true story, USC graduate Shalin Shah leaves behind the expectations of his Indian-American family and his girlfriend Fiona to serve as a Peace Corps volunteer in Peru. But when a persistent cough leads to a devastating diagnosis of synovial sarcoma, a rare and aggressive cancer, Shalin is forced to return home and confront a future he never anticipated. Surrounded by his family, Fiona, and his closest friends, he begins to reconsider what it means to live with purpose when time can no longer be taken for granted. As Shalin’s perspective deepens, his reflections on gratitude, love, and mortality inspire the essay “Thank You, Cancer,” which is published by HuffPost and goes viral with readers around the world. A devastatingly beautiful story of family, resilience, and the lasting impact of one life, Paper Flowers is a reminder to cherish the people we love and the moments that give life meaning. #SunsetsForShalin

event_title: Lockjaw with Sabrina Greco (Filmmaker), Nino Shengelaia (Moderator)
film_description: Six weeks after getting into a drunk driving accident that leaves her jaw wired shut, Rayna tries to have a fun night out with her friends.
event_description: Lockjaw, a New York Premiere co-presented with Women Under The Influence, screens as part of The Downtown Festival. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with filmmaker Sabrina Greco, moderated by Nino Shengelaia (WUTI). The Downtown Festival celebrates independent artists across film, music, art, and culture in New York City, with its film program running October 10–18.

event_title: Rooftop Shots: Closing Night 2026 with Filmmakers
film_description: This program features a collection of new short films, marking the close of Rooftop Films' 30th season. The screening follows a summer of events hosted across the city, promising a standout selection.
event_description: Celebrate the 30th season of Rooftop Films with 'Rooftop Shots: Closing Night 2026,' a special program showcasing new short films. The event includes doors opening at 7:45 PM, live music starting at 8:15 PM, the film screening at 9:00 PM, and a Q&A session with the filmmakers at 10:30 PM, followed by an afterparty. Tickets are $25.00 for General Admission.

event_title: A Bright Future with Lucía Garibaldi (Director)
film_description: Clever, curious and young, lucky Elisa has been selected for work placement in the North. While everything she’s heard about the North seems idyllic, the trouble is that the few people who do go there don’t ever come back.
event_description: The Museum of the Moving Image is hosting a screening of the 2025 sci-fi drama "A Bright Future" as part of the Las Premieres series. The film, directed by Lucía Garibaldi, explores themes of intergenerational sacrifice and rebellion in a dystopian setting. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with director Lucía Garibaldi.

event_title: Watch Me with Filmmakers
film_description: Film follows Isla, an international student struggling to make ends meet. After encouragement from her extroverted best friend Fay, Isla reluctantly enters the world of webcam modeling, initially as a means of survival, which eventually leads to a personal transformation.
event_description: This event features the US premiere screening of the film "Watch Me." The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with the filmmaker, providing an opportunity for attendees to engage directly with the creative team behind the movie.

event_title: Dreams in Nightmares Q&A with Shatara Michelle Ford (Director)
film_description: After an abrupt layoff, Z embarks on a trip across the Midwestern United States in search of a friend who has seemingly disappeared off the grid. Traveling with her two closest friends, these three queer black femmes find their priorities tested as shapeshifting threats in each city expose (inter)personal and ideological fractures.
event_description: Special Guest In-Person Q&A

event_title: Learning to Fly with Max Lowe (Director), Aisha McAdams (Film Participant), Evan Hayes (Producer)
film_description: Aisha McAdams, a former competitive runner turned photographer, embarks on a journey to document the triumphs and struggles of famed ultra trailrunners, including Jim Walmsley and Eszter Csillag. Traveling to mythical races—the Western States Endurance Run in the mountains of eastern California, the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in the French Alps—the film marvels at athletes who maintain their intensity as they run 100 miles of mountain trails while climbing thousands of vertical feet.
event_presenters: Max Lowe (Director), Aisha McAdams (Film Participant), Evan Hayes (Producer)
event_description: Following select screenings of "Learning to Fly," director Max Lowe, film participant Aisha McAdams, and producer Evan Hayes will be present for a Q&A session with the audience.

event_title: How to Divorce During the War with Andrius Blaževicius (Director)
film_title: How to Divorce During the War
film_description: Vilnius 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment for an honest conversation with her husband Vytas about divorcing - just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine goes into full scale. Now they must navigate the process of separation as it collides with a refugee and mid-life crisis.
event_description: The film "How to Divorce During the War," winner of Best Director World Cinema Dramatic at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, opens on Friday, August 21, 2026. A special Q&A session with director Andrius Blaževicius will follow the 6:40 PM screening on the opening day.

event_title: To Use a Mountain with Filmmakers
film_description: Six rural American communities are marked as candidates for an unthinkable fate: their land, a burial ground for 77,000 tons of nuclear waste. Against the impassive logic of government analysis and archives, a people’s history of resistance and stewardship emerges through a visceral journey across the landscapes, ecologies, and personal histories of the candidate sites.
event_description: Experience the New York Theatrical Premiere of "To Use a Mountain," a film exploring the decades-long struggle over nuclear waste disposal. The screening on Friday, August 21st, Saturday, August 22nd, and Sunday, August 23rd, will be followed by a Q&A session. An open-captioned screening is scheduled for Tuesday, August 25th, and a post-screening Q&A will take place on Thursday, August 27th.

film_description: Never Stop Chasing Live Q&A with Reed Timmer, Ken Cole and Kam Stocks

event_title: IT ENDS Q&A with Alexander Ullom (Director)
film_description: A group of recent grads head out on a late night drive for grub, hoping to enjoy one final hangout before their paths diverge. Instead, they accidentally turn onto a never-ending, two-lane hellscape surrounded by untold horrors and cosmic forces beyond their understanding. Cramped together inside a Jeep Cherokee and with the miles stretching infinitely ahead, they face a choice: embrace their new existence or fight to escape it.
event_description: Special Guest In-Person Q&A

event_title: The Python Hunt with Xander Robin (Filmmaker)
film_description: Every year, the Florida government invites the general public to compete in an invasive python removal contest in the Everglades. For ten nights, an eclectic group of hunters confront the dangerous terrain, nocturnal creatures and their own desires.
event_description: The Rockaway Film Festival presents the New York premiere of 'The Python Hunt,' a documentary chronicling the impact of an invasive python species in South Florida. The screening will be followed by a post-screening conversation with filmmaker Xander Robin. Food will be available from Brothers starting at 6:30 PM.

event_title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Bugs We Love(?) with Tommy José Stathes (Historian)
film_title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Bugs We Love(?)
film_description: New York City's prime theatrical showcase of early and classic animated cartoons, featuring vintage 16mm film prints from historian Tommy José Stathes's personal archives. This August, Stathes presents 'Bugs We Love(?)', a selection dedicated to the true stars of summertime: insects. The assortment spans the 1920s through the '50s, showcasing classic characters such as Elmer Fudd, Popeye, Felix the Cat, and Porky Pig.
event_description: This screening of 'Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Bugs We Love(?)' is a special presentation featuring vintage 16mm film prints from the personal archives of historian Tommy José Stathes. Stathes will be present to provide an introduction to the program and participate in a Q&A session after the screening. The collection focuses on insect-themed animated shorts from the 1920s to the 1950s, highlighting classic characters and rare 'orphan films' that are difficult to access elsewhere.

event_title: The Sun Never Sets with Dakota Fanning (Star), Cory Michael Smith (Star)
film_description: Wendy’s life is thrown into chaos when her boyfriend, Jack, who is older and divorced with children, insists they take space to evaluate the relationship. During their break, Wendy runs into her ex, Chuck, forcing them into a volatile triangle.
event_description: Attend a special sneak preview of 'The Sun Never Sets' followed by a Q&A session with the film's stars, Dakota Fanning and Cory Michael Smith. The event offers an opportunity to experience this mumblecore film from director Joe Swanberg and gain insights from the lead actors.

event_title: Atropia with Hailey Gates (Director), Zia Anger
film_description: When an aspiring actress in a military role-playing facility falls in love with a soldier cast as an insurgent, their unsimulated emotions threaten to derail the performance.
event_description: The Rockaway Film Festival will present 'Atropia', a film by Hailey Gates, followed by a post-screening conversation with director Hailey Gates and Zia Anger. Food will be available from Brothers starting at 6:30 PM. The event is part of the Rockaway Film Festival 8.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Hailey Gates (Director), Eric Yue (Cinematographer), Zia Anger

event_title: Pastorale with Edo Choi (Programmer)
film_description: In the mountain village comes a group of young musicians in Tbilisi. Here they are going to relax and rehearse. Sad story about the final rupture occurred, the peasants do not sing beautiful old songs, the musicians play music incomprehensible to them ... Far from the idyllic image of rural life.
event_description: The film Pastorale will be screened as part of the series "Otar Iosseliani: Fables of Modern Life". The screening on Sunday, August 23rd, will include an introduction by programmer Edo Choi.

event_title: Bound with Miss Malice (Performer), K.James (Performer), Nyx Nocturne (Performer), Vigor Mortis (Performer)
film_description: Corky, a tough female ex-convict working on an apartment renovation in a Chicago building, meets a couple living next door, Caesar, a paranoid mobster, and Violet, his seductive girlfriend, who is immediately attracted to her.
event_presenters: Miss Malice (Performer), K.James (Performer), Nyx Nocturne (Performer), Vigor Mortis (Performer)

film_title: Butthole Surfers: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt
film_description: Follows the story of the groundbreaking Texas-based art-punk band founded by frontman Gibby Haynes and guitarist Paul Leary.
event_presenters: Bob Forrest (Moderator), Tom Stern (Director), Paul Leary (Butthole Surfers member), King Coffey (Butthole Surfers member), Jeff Pinkus (Butthole Surfers member), Gibby Haynes (Butthole Surfers member)
event_description: A screening of 'Butthole Surfers: The Hole Truth and Nothing Butt' followed by a live Q&A session. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with filmmaker William Wrubel, moderated by a special guest. event_title: Crash (1996) with Mark Pagán (creator of Other Men Need Help)
film_description: A car crash victim inexplicably finds himself aroused by car accidents and becomes involved with an underground subculture of like-minded souls.

The film explores themes of technology, obsession, and desire through its NC-17 rating, 100-minute runtime, and 35mm format. Crash was a winner of a Special Jury Prize at the 1996 Cannes Film Festival.

film_title: Tracking Shots: Films from the New York Transit Museum Archives
film_description: This event features films from the New York Transit Museum Archives. It provides a unique opportunity to explore cinematic content related to the history and operations of New York's public transit system, offering insights into its rich heritage through archival footage.
event_description: Join Jodi Shapiro, Curator at the New York Transit Museum, for an introduction to "Tracking Shots: Films from the New York Transit Museum Archives." Shapiro, who has been with the museum since 2014 and became Curator in 2021, will provide context for the films. Her expertise spans nearly 200 years of New York's public transit system, and she frequently gives gallery talks, sharing treasures from the museum's extensive collection.

event_title: Moonrise Kingdom with Film Critic and Author
film_description: Set on an island off the coast of New England in the summer of 1965, Moonrise Kingdom tells the story of two twelve-year-olds who fall in love, make a secret pact, and run away together into the wilderness. As various authorities try to hunt them down, a violent storm is brewing off-shore – and the peaceful island community is turned upside down in more ways than anyone can handle.
event_description: A special screening of Wes Anderson's film 'Moonrise Kingdom', co-presented with JCC Manhattan. The event will feature a guest speaker, a Film Critic and Author, providing insights and discussion. This program is supported by public funds from the NYC Department of Youth and Community Development, in partnership with the City Council and the office of NY City Councilperson Shaun Abreu.

event_title: Come What May with Lahna Turner (co-director and co-producer), Rich Vos (comedian)
film_description: Come What May tells the full story of Ralphie May through the comics who stood beside him, the friends who knew him best, and the people who watched him burn bright at the center of comedy.

event_description: Experience an unflinching portrait of comedian Ralphie May, featuring candid interviews and never-before-seen archival footage. The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with co-director and co-producer Lahna Turner and comedian Rich Vos.

event_title: In the Family with Patrick Wang (Director)
film_description: In the town of Martin, Tennessee, Chip Hines, a precocious six year old, has only known life with his two dads, Cody and Joey. And a good life it is. When Cody dies suddenly in a car accident, Joey and Chip struggle to find their footing again. Just as they begin to, Cody's will reveals that he named his sister as Chip's guardian. The years of Joey's acceptance into the family unravel as Chip is taken away from him. In his now solitary home life, Joey searches for a solution. The law is not on his side, but friends are. Armed with their comfort and inspired by memories of Cody, Joey finds a path to peace with the family and closer to his son.
event_description: Following a 35MM screening of 'In the Family', actor/director Patrick Wang will partake in a post-screening Q&A session.

event_title: Escape from L.A. with Martin Monster
film_description: Into the 9.6-quaked Los Angeles of 2013 comes Snake Plissken. His job: wade through L.A.'s ruined landmarks to retrieve a doomsday device.
event_description: This screening of "Escape from L.A." will feature an introduction by Brooklyn’s favorite horror host, pop culture connoisseur, and eternal singing, dancing misanthrope, Martin Monster. The film is presented in 35mm format.

event_title: IF I TELL YOU Q&A
film_description: IF I TELL YOU uncovers a family’s pressing secret while the 12-year-old son finds his voice and the courage to stand up for what is right.

event_title: Trapped: Mind-Altering Shorts with Filmmakers
film_description: Blending horror, satire, surrealism, and psychological unease, this collection of shorts delves into unsettling realms where reality distorts, bodies transform, and established beliefs unravel. The program promises a disorienting journey as perceptions shift and the familiar becomes frighteningly ambiguous.
event_description: This event features a program of mind-altering short films exploring themes of horror, satire, surrealism, and psychological unease, followed by a Q&A session with the filmmakers. Attendees can anticipate a dive into worlds where reality is challenged and perceptions are twisted. Doors open at 7:00 PM, with films beginning at 8:30 PM.

event_title: Filipina with Rafael Manuel (Filmmaker)
film_description: Isabel feels strangely drawn to Dr. Palanca, the president of the country club where she works. However, after piecing together a violent picture of what lies beneath the club’s pristine surface, she realizes that what began as an innocent infatuation is actually rooted in a sinister shared history.
event_description: Filipina will be screened followed by a Q&A session with writer, director, and editor Rafael Manuel. Manuel, based between Amsterdam, London, and Manila, is celebrated for his short films, which have earned accolades including a Silver Bear at the Berlinale and screenings at prestigious festivals such as Locarno, IFFR, and FIDMarseilles. This event marks the debut feature-length film for Manuel, who was also mentored by Jia Zhang-ke as the last film protege at the Rolex Arts Initiative.

event_title: Boorman and the Devil with David Kittredge (Director)
film_description: Featuring commentary from surviving participants, as well as other filmmakers and critics, this documentary chronicles the career of director John Boorman and the tumultuous production of his film Exorcist II: The Heretic, exploring its critical and commercial failure, how it changed the industry, and the importance of risk-taking in art.
event_description: Experience screenings of 'Boorman and the Devil', a documentary detailing the challenging production of John Boorman's 'Exorcist II: The Heretic'. Each screening will be followed by a Q&A session featuring director David Kittredge, offering insights into the film and its subject matter.

event_title: Ganz + Streeter, PGM 1: New Discoveries with Tony Ganz, Rhody Streeter
film_description: This program presents a collection of new discoveries from filmmakers Tony Ganz and Rhody Streeter. It features a selection of their early works and collaborative pieces, offering insights into their distinctive styles and thematic explorations. The films delve into various subjects, capturing moments from daily life to broader cultural observations.
event_description: This screening showcases new discoveries from the works of Tony Ganz and Rhody Streeter, including individual projects like 'The New Deal' and 'Claremont Stables,' as well as their collaborations such as 'Y.E.S.' and 'Muzak.' The program also features an excerpt from their episode on Robert Gardner’s interview program, 'Screening Room.' Both Tony Ganz and Rhody Streeter will be present for Q&A sessions after the screenings on August 28 and 29.

event_title: Top of the World with Filmmakers
film_description: Explores Windows on the World, the iconic restaurant that occupied the 106th and 107th floors of the North Tower of the World Trade Center.
event_description: Experience the world premiere of "Top of the World," a poignant documentary directed by Julie Cohen and Betsy West. The film tells the story of Windows on the World, the iconic restaurant atop the World Trade Center, and its diverse staff who were tragically lost on 9/11. Several screenings include a Q&A session, offering an opportunity to delve deeper into the film's themes and production. Doors open 30 minutes prior to showtime, and concessions are available to support the nonprofit venue.

event_title: The Cycle of Love with Orlando von Einsiedel (Filmmaker), P.K. Mahanandia (Film Participant), Lotta Mahanandia (Film Participant)
film_description: Explores the romantic journey of PK Mahanandia, a Delhi street artist who trekked 6,000 miles by bicycle in 1977, venturing across continents to reunite with the woman he loved.
event_presenters: Orlando von Einsiedel (Filmmaker), P.K. Mahanandia (Film Participant), Lotta Mahanandia (Film Participant)
event_description: Screenings of THE CYCLE OF LOVE will be followed by a Q&A session with filmmaker Orlando von Einsiedel and film participants P.K. Mahanandia and Lotta Mahanandia on opening weekend, Friday, August 28th and Saturday, August 29th, after the 7:10 PM shows.

event_title: The Black Dahlia with Stephanie Monohan
film_description: In 1940s Los Angeles, two former boxers-turned-cops must grapple with corruption, narcissism, stag films and family madness as they pursue the killer of an aspiring young actress.
event_description: Experience a 35MM screening of Brian De Palma's 2006 thriller, "The Black Dahlia," as part of the “2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die” series, curated by Steve Macfarlane. The screening on August 28 will include an introduction by Stephanie Monohan.

event_title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets with Kevin Walker (Introduction)
film_description: Benjamin Franklin Gates and Abigail Chase re-team with Riley Poole and, now armed with a stack of long-lost pages from John Wilkes Booth's diary, Ben must follow a clue left there to prove his ancestor's innocence in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
event_description: Experience Jon Turteltaub's 2007 film, "National Treasure: Book of Secrets," presented on a near-pristine 35mm print from the Disney archive. The screening on Friday, August 28, will feature an introduction by Kevin Walker, offering additional insights into this action-adventure sequel.

event_title: Secrets & Lies with Shay Filmore
film_description: After her adoptive mother dies, Hortense, a successful black optometrist, seeks out her birth mother. She's shocked when her research leads her to Cynthia, a working class white woman.
event_description: This screening of Mike Leigh's 1996 Palme d’Or winner, Secrets & Lies, is part of the "My First Time" film series. It is introduced by Shay Filmore, who will be watching the film for the first time. The event highlights Marianne Jean-Baptiste's praise of Leigh’s improvisational rehearsal processes, inspired by her recent work on 2024’s Hard Truths.

event_title: The Kill-Off + My New Gun with Maggie Greenwald, Stacy Cochran
film_description: Film at Lincoln Center presents a special 2-for-1 35mm double feature of the seminal New Jersey–set noirs, The Kill-Off and My New Gun. This event also includes a panel discussion with Greenwald, Cochran, and other members of Missing Movies to raise awareness about the organization’s ongoing work.
event_description: This event is a 2-for-1 35mm double feature of two New Jersey-set noirs, The Kill-Off and My New Gun. Following the screening of The Kill-Off, there will be a Missing Movies panel discussion featuring Maggie Greenwald, Stacy Cochran, and other members of the organization, aiming to raise awareness about their ongoing efforts to advocate for and preserve missing films.

event_title: The Warriors with Michael Gingold (Author), Chris Poggiali (Author)
film_description: Prominent gang leader Cyrus calls a meeting of New York's gangs to set aside their turf wars and take over the city. At the meeting, a rival leader kills Cyrus, but a Coney Island gang called the Warriors is wrongly blamed for Cyrus' death. Before you know it, the cops and every gangbanger in town is hot on the Warriors' trail.
event_description: The screening of "The Warriors" will be introduced by authors Michael Gingold and Chris Poggiali, who will also be signing copies of their book, "Armies of the Night: THE WARRIORS and Its Legacy," in the lobby at 8:00 PM before the screening. This event is part of the "NYC IN TRANSIT" series. Michael Gingold, a former editor for Fangoria, and Chris Poggiali, a librarian and film historian, are both experts in horror and cult films.

event_title: Stepping Into the Unknown: films from the Bob Dylan Center with Steven Jenkins (Director), Steve Wynn (Musician)
film_title: Stepping Into the Unknown: films from the Bob Dylan Center
film_description: The Bob Dylan Center presents a far-ranging one-hour program of short films and videos from the Bob Dylan Archive featuring rare and previously unreleased clips of Dylan on stage and in the studio. Spanning decades and musical styles, this compendium of clips highlights Dylan’s arrival in Greenwich Village and his early protest songs. Selections include Dylan’s first film soundtrack for 1961’s “Autopsy on Operation Abolition;” a devastating solo rendition of “Ballad of Hollis Brown;” a rollicking 1976 take on “I Pity the Poor Immigrant” with Joan Baez; a gospel-infused “Blowin’ in the Wind;” a loving tribute to Tony Bennett; a glimpse into the Archive’s film restoration project with never-before-seen footage of “It’s All Over Now, Baby Blue” from 1966; and, in keeping with the season, a look at the making of Dylan’s yuletide album “Christmas in the Heart.”
event_description: Bob Dylan Center Director Steven Jenkins will present an all-new collection of rare Dylan films, followed by a post-screening discussion and audience Q&A with singer-songwriter Steve Wynn. Wynn will conclude the program with a brief set of Dylan covers.

event_title: New York, New York with Griffin Newman (Blank Check podcast), David Sims (Blank Check podcast)
film_description: An egotistical saxophone player and a young singer meet on V-J Day and embark upon a strained and rocky romance, even as their careers begin a long uphill climb.
event_presenters: Griffin Newman (Blank Check podcast), David Sims (Blank Check podcast)
event_description: Experience Martin Scorsese's "New York, New York" with a special introduction by Griffin Newman and David Sims of the Blank Check podcast. The film is presented in 35mm format and features Liza Minnelli and Robert De Niro.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Griffin Newman (Blank Check podcast), David Sims (Blank Check podcast)

event_title: Stepping into the Unknown: Films from the Bob Dylan Center with Steven Jenkins (Director of the Bob Dylan Center), Elvis Costello (Musician)
film_title: Stepping into the Unknown: Films from the Bob Dylan Center
film_description: This one-hour program showcases a diverse collection of short films and videos from the Bob Dylan Archive, spanning decades and musical styles. It features rare and previously unreleased clips of Dylan onstage and in the studio, alongside selections like his first film soundtrack and live performances with iconic artists such as Joan Baez and Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers. The collection also includes tributes to Johnny Cash and Tony Bennett, providing a comprehensive look into Dylan's extensive career and the Archive's restoration efforts.
event_presenters: Steven Jenkins (Director of the Bob Dylan Center), Elvis Costello (Musician)
event_description: A screening of 'Stepping Into the Unknown: Films from the Bob Dylan Center' will be followed by an onstage conversation. The discussion will feature Steven Jenkins, Director of the Bob Dylan Center, and musician Elvis Costello. The program itself is a one-hour compilation of rare and unreleased short films and videos from the Bob Dylan Archive, highlighting various aspects of Dylan's career through different musical styles and decades.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Steven Jenkins (Director, Bob Dylan Center), Bill Frisell (Musician)

event_title: Wiseman’s New York with Genevieve Yue
film_description: This immersive, 10-day mini-lab invites participants to explore the precise and generously observed body of work from Frederick Wiseman, studying New York City through the lens of one of documentary's most formidable figures. The program includes comprehensive surveys by top scholars and experts, alongside opportunities to visit the institutions, neighborhoods, and civic spaces documented in his films.
event_description: Join an immersive 10-day mini-lab dedicated to the works of master documentarian Frederick Wiseman, focusing on his nine films set in New York City. The program features public screenings of these monumental films at cinemas across the city, seminars, panels, and field trips led by esteemed film scholar Genevieve Yue and other experts. Participants can dive deep into Wiseman's singular approach to observation, civic engagement, and documentary practice, experiencing New York as a living classroom.

event_title: Wiseman’s New York with Genevieve Yue
film_description: This mini-lab offers an immersive tour of New York City through the precise and generously observed body of work from Frederick Wiseman, one of documentary’s most formidable figures. Participants will study the city through his lens, with comprehensive surveys and invitations to visit documented institutions and civic spaces. The program includes public screenings of his nine New York films at various city cinemas.
event_description: This 10-day mini-lab provides an immersive exploration of Frederick Wiseman’s films about New York City, featuring public screenings, seminars, panels, and field trips. Esteemed film scholar Genevieve Yue leads the program, joined by filmmakers, critics, artists, and community members who will discuss Wiseman's unique approach to documentary filmmaking and civic engagement. The event is a unique opportunity to engage with his monumental body of work within a supportive, discursive community at some of the city’s finest cinematic institutions.

event_title: Eternity One with Marnie Ellen Hertzler (Filmmaker)
film_description: ETERNITY ONE follows Mary Ella, a young girl growing up on Tangier Island in the Chesapeake Bay, where rising seas have already claimed two-thirds of the land and threaten to erase what remains. Once a thriving fishing community, Tangier now faces the collapse of both home and livelihood.
event_description: This screening of "Eternity One" will be followed by a Q&A session with the filmmaker, Marnie Ellen Hertzler. The film explores the personal and intimate world of a young girl on Tangier Island as it faces the threat of rising seas.

event_title: The Matter Propounded: Three Films by David Gatten with David Gatten
film_title: The Matter Propounded: Three Films by David Gatten
film_description: Across three films, American experimental filmmaker David Gatten moves from a 17th-century dream of total knowledge, through a manual for divining the future, to a forbidden love that survives only in fragments. Working across handmade 16mm and digital media, Gatten sets printed matter and obsolete systems in motion, drawing out their visual and material possibilities while attending to how forms of writing now strange to us once helped people make sense of their lives.
event_description: This screening presents three films by David Gatten: 'The Great Art of Knowing,' 'The Matter Propounded: Of Its Possibility or Impossibility, Treated in Four Parts,' and 'What Places of Heaven, What Planets Directed, How Long the Effects? or, The General Accidents of the World.' Following the screening, David Gatten will participate in a Q&A session. The runtime for the films is 79 minutes and they are presented in 16mm format.

event_title: The Room with Greg Sestero (Star)
film_description: Johnny is a successful banker with great respect for and dedication to the people in his life, especially his future wife Lisa. The happy-go-lucky guy sees his world being torn apart when his friends begin to betray him one-by-one.
event_description: Join us for a special evening featuring a screening of "The Room," followed by a live script reading and a Q&A session with star Greg Sestero. Greg Sestero is also the New York Times bestselling author of "The Disaster Artist."

event_title: A Page of Madness with Order of the Illusive (Live Musical Accompaniment)
film_description: A man takes a job at an asylum with hopes of freeing his imprisoned wife.
event_presenters: Order of the Illusive (Live Musical Accompaniment)
event_description: This screening of Teinosuke Kinugasa's groundbreaking Japanese silent film, A Page of Madness, features a live original score by Order of the Illusive. Celebrating its 100th anniversary this year, the film's dreamlike imagery and psychological intensity are complemented by the trio's immersive blend of ambient textures, experimental rock, improvisation, and cinematic soundscapes. Order of the Illusive, formed in 2012, creates live, improvised experimental scores for silent films, using electric guitar, pencilina, 17-string bass, electronics, and percussion.

event_title: Shorts: Wired + Wide-Eyed with Filmmakers
film_description: Short dramas that are reckless and combustible, these films are fueled by the energy of adolescence. They reverse roles and flip power dynamics inside out, offering a dynamic exploration of youthful intensity.
event_description: A program of short dramas titled 'Wired + Wide-Eyed,' characterized by their reckless and combustible nature. These films draw energy from adolescence, showcasing reversed roles and flipped power dynamics. The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with filmmakers.

event_title: The Night is Fading Away with Ramiro Sonzini (Filmmaker)
film_description: Pelu is a thirty-something who barely survives on his salary as a projectionist at a municipal film club. After losing his job, he agrees to stay on as a night watchman and ends up living secretly inside the cinema, accompanied by the films he reviews every night.
event_description: The Night is Fading Away will be screened, followed by a Q&A session with filmmaker Ramiro Sonzini. The evening will begin with music by Frances Chang and food provided by Delroy Delectables, in partnership with Istic Illic.

event_title: Chronovisor with Kevin Walker (Director), Jack Auen (Director)
film_description: A French academic is seduced into a world of untold histories in her scholarly quest to uncover the mystery of a history-capturing camera-like machine created by clandestine Benedictine monks. An academic-noir, armchair mystery in the lineage of Jorge Luis Borges and Umberto Eco.
event_description: The North American Premiere of Chronovisor, a film by Kevin Walker and Jack Auen, will include a screening followed by a Q&A session with the filmmakers. The movie is part of the New Directors/New Films 2026 festival.

event_title: High School II with Genevieve Yue (Presenter)
film_description: HIGH SCHOOL II is a film about Central Park East Secondary School (CPESS), a successful alternative high school in New York's Spanish Harlem, 85-95% of whose graduates go on to four year colleges. The film illustrates the school's emphasis on the “Habits of Mind” program (weighing evidence; awareness of multiple points of view; seeing connections and relationships; speculating on possibilities; and assessing values.) Sequences illustrating the school's approach to learning include: classroom activities in the humanities and sciences; family conferences; discussions of race, class, and gender; faculty meetings; disciplinary problems; sex education; conflict resolution by students; and student council meetings.
event_description: This special screening of Frederick Wiseman’s High School II is presented as part of the “Wiseman’s New York” program, an immersive survey and seminar series exploring Wiseman’s New York films and the civic spaces they document. The event includes an introduction by Genevieve Yue.

event_title: Shorts: Romantasy with Nora Rodriguez (Curator), Sim Hahahah, Karen Leo
film_description: This program presents a collection of animations that explore themes of longing, waiting, and watching, echoing the modern literary genre of 'romantasy.' Drawing inspiration from fan fiction and popular culture, these animated shorts offer a surprisingly dark, obsessive, and dystopian yet utterly delightful viewing experience.
event_presenters: Nora Rodriguez (Curator), Sim Hahahah, Karen Leo
event_description: Guest curated by Nora Rodriguez, 'Shorts: Romantasy' is a screening of animations about longing, waiting, and watching. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with Nora Rodriguez, Sim Hahahah, and Karen Leo. The evening concludes with live music performed by the Rockaway roots reggae band Foundation in the courtyard.

event_title: Ulysses, New York with Caveh Zahedi (Filmmaker), Katie Way (Moderator), original cast members
film_description: New York independent filmmaker and provocateur Caveh Zahedi explores truth by filming his entire life. In 2022, he undertook a challenging, low-budget production of James Joyce's Ulysses, with limited time for writing, casting, and rehearsals. This work-in-progress version of the first chapter showcases the chaotic process in Zahedi's intensely confessional and self-reflexive style.
event_presenters: Caveh Zahedi (Filmmaker), Katie Way (Moderator), original cast members
event_description: The event features a work-in-progress screening of the first chapter of Caveh Zahedi's 'Ulysses, New York', an ambitious adaptation of James Joyce's novel. Prior to the screening, Zahedi will present a unique theatrical performance. Following the film, there will be a panel discussion with members of the original cast, moderated by Katie Way from Hell Gate, and food will be provided by Bunna. This event is presented in partnership with Hell Gate and is part of the Rockaway Film Festival #9.

film_description: This musical mayhem is an outrageous assemblage of stereotyped science fiction movies, Marvel comics, Frankie Avalon/Annette Funicello outings, and rock 'n' roll of every vintage.
