event_title: Model with Genevieve Yue
film_description: MODEL shows male and female models at work on TV commercials, fashion shows, magazine covers, and advertising for a variety of products, including designer collections, fur coats, sports clothes and automobiles. The models are seen at work with photographers whose techniques illustrate different styles of fashion and product photography. The business aspect of running an agency is also shown: interviewing prospective models, career counseling, arranging portfolios, talking with clients, and planning trips. The film presents a view of the intersections of fashion, business, advertising, photography, television and fantasy.
event_description: UnionDocs presents a special screening of Frederick Wiseman’s "Model" as part of the "Wiseman’s New York" program. This 10-day event includes an immersive survey and seminars on Wiseman’s New York films, alongside visits to the institutions, neighborhoods, and civic spaces documented in his work. The screening of "Model" will be accompanied by Genevieve Yue, an associate professor of culture and media at The New School, who will contribute to the program.

event_title: The Muppet Movie with Bonnie Erickson (Puppet Designer)
film_description: The Muppets gather to watch their newly-finished big-budget rich-and-famous feature film: a talent agent persuades Kermit the Frog to leave the swamp to pursue a career in Hollywood. On his way there, he meets a bear, a pig, a whatever (his future muppet crew), and some special celebrity guest stars, while being chased by the desperate owner of a frog-leg restaurant!
event_description: Experience 'The Muppet Movie,' a cinematic journey from television to the big screen, featuring a post-screening conversation with Bonnie Erickson, legendary puppet designer and creator of Miss Piggy. This event is part of the Rockaway Film Festival #9 and is presented as Free Children’s Cinema in partnership with the Mayor's Office of Media and Entertainment.

event_title: The Infra-ordinary with Jenny Odell (Guest Curator)
film_description: These films question the life and liveliness of things, hovering between the magical promise of the consumer product and the terrible ordinariness of refuse. The curated collection draws inspiration from Georges Perec's instruction to "Question your tea spoons" in his book L’Infra-ordinaire.
event_description: The event features a guest-curated program of shorts titled "The Infra-ordinary," by Jenny Odell. The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with Odell, a former arts educator and author, known for her books focusing on resisting the attention economy and discovering life beyond the clock. Her work often explores the ordinary and overlooked aspects of everyday objects and systems.

event_title: The History of Concrete with John Wilson
film_description: After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, filmmaker John Wilson tries to use the same formula to sell a documentary about concrete.
event_description: An advance screening of John Wilson's debut feature, "The History of Concrete," will be held at the Arverne Cinema. The event includes music by Heems, followed by the screening, and a Q&A session with John Wilson. Food will be provided by La Cevicheria, and a ticket includes access to an after-party with Nebulus. The event is presented in partnership with BjornQorn and is part of the Rockaway Film Festival #9.

event_title: Adnan Being and Time with Marie Valentine Regan (Filmmaker)
film_description: An expressionistic portrait of Etel Adnan, immersed in her art and the world. Working without ego, Adnan asks, what does it mean to be alive, to live through catastrophe, to experience time.
event_description: Experience a screening of 'Adnan Being and Time,' a portrait of Lebanese-American poet and artist Etel Adnan. The film captures Adnan's final years, offering insights into her life and art. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with filmmaker Marie Valentine Regan.

event_title: Shorts: Knowledge Across Bodies with Ramón Rivera Moret, Mars Verrone
film_description: Charting alternate maps into unknown territories, these short films navigate the natural world across geologies and generations. This program features four distinct shorts, offering diverse perspectives on knowledge and the human experience within the natural world.
event_description: A screening of 'Shorts: Knowledge Across Bodies' will be held as part of the Rockaway Film Festival #9. This program includes four short films: 'Æquo' by Julia Borderie + Éloïse Le Gallo (2023, France, 20 min), 'La dirección del cielo I, Bernardino' by Ramón Rivera Moret (2026, Peru, 13 min), 'The Creature of Darkness' by Lisa Marie Malloy + Ray Whitaker (2026, US, 15 min), and 'Buckskin' by Mars Verrone (2026, US, 17 min). The event will feature a Q&A session with filmmakers Ramón Rivera Moret and Mars Verrone.

event_title: Peter Hutton: On the Hudson with Ed Halter (Introducer)
film_description: Visionary American filmmaker Peter Hutton presents a selection of 16mm films. A former merchant seaman, Hutton spent nearly forty years voyaging the world, often aboard cargo ships, recording the places he visited in exquisite, silent diaries. Drawing from nineteenth-century landscape painting and traditions of early cinema, Hutton distilled the natural world into images of a rare and quiet awe.
event_description: For the closing night program of Rockaway Film Festival #9, a selection of 16mm films by Peter Hutton will be screened, focusing on the Hudson River. The evening will include music by White Magic, an introduction by Ed Halter, and food by Brothers. A closing night party hosted by Light and Sound Design, KG, and Friends is included with the ticket.

event_title: The Paper (纸) with Ding Jiancheng (Director)
film_description: The story is set in a small village in South-Eastern China, during the Cultural Revolution. A teenager is bored and spends most of his time hanging around in the street. An old man, a widower, earns his money making artistic paper shapes of people, animals, vehicles, and other things. It is an old custom to burn these pieces of paper as a sacrifice to the dead — but in the years of the Cultural Revolution, this was regarded as superstition, and banned. The old man uses dazibao, propaganda posters, and secretly makes them into figures that should be burnt on his death. One day, the teenager accompanies the old man to his house and finds out the old man's secret. A bond ensues between the two. The boy finds out that the man once had a daughter, Qingqing, who was hit in the forties by a stray bullet. Since then, he has always dreamt about the beauty of Qingqing.
event_description: Experience a screening of Ding Jiancheng's acclaimed film, The Paper (纸), a visually unique Chinese film from 1993, as part of the 'Chinese Artists on the Edge' series. The film, recently digitized by the Asian Film Archive, will be followed by a Q&A session with director Ding Jiancheng. Complimentary tickets are available for NYC college students with ID at the box office on the day of the screening.

event_title: Netflix's Fauda Season 5 with Lior Raz (Co-creator, Star), Avi Issacharoff (Co-creator), Bianna Golodryga (Moderator)
film_description: The acclaimed Israeli action-drama returns for a fifth season, featuring the screening of its first two episodes. The series delves into the aftermath of a tragedy two years prior, as the Fauda unit grapples with a quest for vengeance that transforms into a perilous mission to avert a major terrorist attack.
event_presenters: Lior Raz (Co-creator, Star), Avi Issacharoff (Co-creator), Bianna Golodryga (Moderator)
event_description: This event features a screening of the first two episodes of Fauda Season 5, followed by a conversation with co-creators Lior Raz, who also stars in the series, and Avi Issacharoff. The discussion, moderated by CNN’s Bianna Golodryga, will explore the making of the new season, the events that shaped its story, and the challenges of creating an action thriller amidst evolving real-world contexts.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Lior Raz (Co-creator, Star), Avi Issacharoff (Co-creator), Bianna Golodryga (Moderator)

event_title: The 2026 Etheria Film Festival Short Film Showcase with Sandra Powers (Filmmaker), Kara Grace Miller (Filmmaker), Christianne Hedtke (Filmmaker), Kristina Klebe (Filmmaker)
film_title: The 2026 Etheria Film Festival Short Film Showcase
film_description: The world's most loved and respected film festival showcase of new horror, science fiction, and fantasy films directed by women. Etheria has a 12-year history of discovering and launching the careers of masters of horror such as Axelle Carolyn, Gigi Saul Guerrero, Chloe Okuno, Mariama Diallo, Roseanne Liang, Natalie Erika James, and Prano Bailey-Bond.
event_presenters: Sandra Powers (Filmmaker), Kara Grace Miller (Filmmaker), Christianne Hedtke (Filmmaker), Kristina Klebe (Filmmaker)
event_description: The Etheria Film Festival, celebrating its 12th year, presents its official 2026 showcase lineup featuring new horror, science fiction, and fantasy films directed by women. The screening includes a Q&A session with filmmakers Sandra Powers, Kara Grace Miller, Christianne Hedtke, and Kristina Klebe. The event will be preceded by trailers for new feature films NOXTURNE, directed by Kristina Klebe, and LAST CHANCE MOTEL, directed by Danielle Harris and Scout Taylor-Compton. The festival is co-presented by Brooklyn Horror Film Festival and The Future of Film is Female.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Sandra Powers (Filmmaker), Kara Grace Miller (Filmmaker), Christianne Hedtke (Filmmaker), Kristina Klebe (Filmmaker)

event_title: The Oldest Person in the World with Sam Green (Director)
film_title: The Oldest Person in the World
film_description: A decade-long global journey chronicles the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate, and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.
event_description: Opening weekend screenings of 'The Oldest Person in the World' at Angelika Film Center will feature a Q&A session with director Sam Green following the 7:00 PM shows on Thursday, September 10th; Friday, September 11th; and Saturday, September 12th. The film explores the lives of various individuals who have held the title of the oldest living person, evolving into a broader reflection on time and human experience.

event_title: Marie Antoinette with Sofia Coppola (Filmmaker)
film_description: A retelling of the story of France’s iconic but ill-fated queen, Marie Antoinette - from her betrothal and marriage to Louis XVI at fifteen to her reign as queen at nineteen and ultimately the fall of Versailles.
event_description: The film "Marie Antoinette" will be screened, followed by a Q&A session with filmmaker Sofia Coppola. The screening will mark the New York Premiere of a newly restored 4K version of the film, commemorating its 20th anniversary.

event_title: The Gentlemen with Theo James (Star), Kaya Scodelario (Star)
film_description: American expat Mickey Pearson has built a highly profitable marijuana empire in London. When word gets out that he’s looking to cash out of the business forever it triggers plots, schemes, bribery and blackmail in an attempt to steal his domain out from under him.
event_description: This event features a screening of an episode from the new season of Netflix’s action-comedy series The Gentlemen. Following the screening, stars Theo James and Kaya Scodelario will engage in a conversation about the new season, discussing the show's blend of crime and comedy, their experiences inhabiting Guy Ritchie’s fast-talking universe, and stories from the set.

event_title: On a String with Isabel Hagen
film_description: A young, Juilliard-trained violist is still living at home with her parents in the heart of NYC, while trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends in the homes of strangers.
event_description: The screening of "On a String" on Friday, September 11, will be followed by a Q&A session with Isabel Hagen.

event_title: Another Day in Paradise with Larry Clark (Director)
film_description: In the hope of a big score, two junkie couples team up to commit various drug robberies which go disastrously wrong, leading to dissent, violence, and murder.
event_description: A special 35MM screening of 'Another Day in Paradise' will be held, followed by an in-person appearance and discussion with director Larry Clark.

event_title: Viva Las Vegas with Sam Taffel, Gillian Waldo
film_description: Lucky Jackson arrives in Las Vegas with his car literally in tow ready for the first Grand Prix — once he has the money for an engine. He gets the cash easily enough but mislays it when the pretty pool manageress takes his mind off things. It seems he'll lose both race and girl, problems complicated by rivalry from womanizing fellow racer Elmo Mancini.
event_description: Experience a special 35MM presentation of the classic musical-comedy 'Viva Las Vegas,' preceded by 'Learning from Learning from Las Vegas,' an experimental adaptation of the seminal architectural text. The event on September 12th includes a Q&A session with Sam Taffel and Gillian Waldo, the filmmakers behind the preceding short.

event_title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day One with Filmmakers
film_title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day One
film_description: Junk Dump Magazine's sixth annual short film festival highlights emerging and underrepresented filmmakers working at the intersection of video art and storytelling. This curated program presents narrative, animated, and experimental short films by artists using unique processes to tell engaging stories. The selection for this year was guest judged and curated by New York-based filmmakers Caroline Mariko Stucky and Sidney Rose White.
event_description: The Museum of the Moving Image and Junk Dump Magazine present Day One of the Junk Dump Film Festival 2026, featuring a selection of seven narrative and documentary shorts. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with the filmmakers. The festival aims to showcase emerging and underrepresented filmmakers, presenting a curated program of innovative short films.

event_title: The Departed - 35MM with Toney J. Brown
film_description: An undercover cop and a mole in the police attempt to identify each other while infiltrating an Irish gang in South Boston. The film is part of the “2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die” series.
event_description: The Departed, a 2006 crime drama, will be screened as part of the “2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die” series, curated by Steve Macfarlane. The screening on September 13th will include an introduction by Toney J. Brown.

event_title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day Two with Filmmakers
film_title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day Two
film_description: Museum of the Moving Image and Junk Dump Magazine present the sixth annual Junk Dump short film festival. The festival highlights emerging and underrepresented filmmakers working at the intersection of video art and storytelling, featuring a curated program of narrative, animated, and experimental short films.
event_description: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day Two features a selection of nine experimental and animated shorts, curated by Caroline Mariko Stucky and Sidney Rose White. The screening will be followed by a Q&A session with the filmmakers. The program has a run time of approximately 80 minutes.

event_title: Mississippi Triangle with JT Takagi (Executive Director, Third World Newsreel), Yuet Fung Ho (Associate Producer)
film_description: This is an intimate portrait of life in the Mississippi Delta, where Chinese, African Americans and Whites live in a complex world of cotton, work, and racial conflict. The history of the Chinese community is framed against the harsh realities of civil , religion, politics, and class in the South. Rare historical footage and interviews of Delta residents are combined to create this unprecedented document of inter-ethnic relations in the American South.
event_presenters: JT Takagi (Executive Director, Third World Newsreel), Yuet Fung Ho (Associate Producer)
event_description: Experience the film 'Mississippi Triangle' as part of the Christine Choy Retrospective. Each screening will be followed by a Q&A session. The Monday, September 14th screening will feature a Q&A with JT Takagi (Executive Director, Third World Newsreel) and Yuet Fung Ho (Associate Producer). The Wednesday, September 16th screening will include a Q&A with JT Takagi, Yuet Fung Ho, and Dr. Josslyn Luckett (Screenwriter, Scholar, Cinema Studies Professor at NYU).

screenings.in_person_appearence: JT Takagi (Executive Director, Third World Newsreel), Yuet Fung Ho (Associate Producer)
JT Takagi (Executive Director, Third World Newsreel), Yuet Fung Ho (Associate Producer), Dr. Josslyn Luckett (Screenwriter, Scholar, Cinema Studies Professor at NYU)

event_title: To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar with Miss Malice (Performer), Daniella Darling (Performer), C'était Bontemps (Performer), Sherry Poppins (Performer)
film_title: To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar
film_description: Manhattan drag queens Vida Boheme and Noxeema Jackson impress regional judges in competition, securing berths in the Nationals in Los Angeles. When the two meet pathetic drag novice Chi-Chi Rodriguez — one of the losers that evening — the charmed Vida and Noxeema agree to take the hopeless youngster under their joined wing. Soon the three set off on a madcap road trip across America and struggle to make it to Los Angeles in time.
event_presenters: Miss Malice (Performer), Daniella Darling (Performer), C'était Bontemps (Performer), Sherry Poppins (Performer)
event_description: Experience a special screening of "To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar" featuring a live pre-show drag performance by Miss Malice, accompanied by special guests Daniella Darling, C'était Bontemps, and Sherry Poppins. This event also supports The Okra Project, a Black trans-led organization.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Miss Malice (Performer), Daniella Darling (Performer), C'était Bontemps (Performer), Sherry Poppins (Performer)

event_title: White Nights with Isabella Rossellini (Actor)
film_description: After his plane crashes in Siberia, a Russian dancer, who defected to the West, is held prisoner in the Soviet Union. The KGB keeps him under watch and tries to convince him to become a dancer for the Kirov Academy of Ballet again. Determined to escape, he befriends a black American expatriate and his pregnant Russian wife, who agree to help him escape to the American Embassy.
event_description: The film "White Nights" will be screened as the closing night feature, presented in 70mm, marking its first such screening in NYC in over four decades. Actor Isabella Rossellini will be present for a Q&A session following the screening.

event_title: Une femme coquette, A Day in the Country with The Crimson Curtain with Michael Witt (Professor and Author)
film_title: Une femme coquette, A Day in the Country with The Crimson Curtain
film_description: This screening presents three distinct short films: Jean-Luc Godard's ultra-rare earliest short 'Une femme coquette', Jean Renoir's deeply sensuous 'A Day in the Country', and Alexandre Astruc's acclaimed 'The Crimson Curtain'. The program highlights literary adaptations and Godard's early influences, connecting these works through shared inspirations from authors like Guy de Maupassant.
event_description: This event features a screening of three films: 'Une femme coquette' (Dir. Jean-Luc Godard, 1954, 10min, DCP), 'A Day in the Country' (Dir. Jean Renoir, 1936, 41 min, DCP), and 'The Crimson Curtain' (Dir. Alexandre Astruc, 1953, 44 min, 35mm). The 7 PM screening will be introduced and followed by a conversation with Michael Witt, a professor and author, who curated this series focusing on literary adaptation and Jean-Luc Godard's influences.

event_title: Soul Patrol with J.M. Harper (Filmmaker)
film_description: From deep behind enemy lines, a hidden chapter of American military history is uncovered, prompting the question of whether reckoning with the past can bring peace to those who lived it. The Vietnam War’s first Black special operations team reunites to tell their story.
event_description: The NYC premiere of the Sundance-winning film Soul Patrol will be followed by an on-stage conversation with filmmaker J.M. Harper. This special screening is part of DOC NYC SELECTS, an ongoing screening series that extends DOC NYC's annual fall festival.

event_title: A Scanner Darkly with Alex Lei
film_description: An undercover cop in a not-too-distant future becomes involved with a dangerous new drug and begins to lose his own identity as a result.
event_description: Experience Richard Linklater's "A Scanner Darkly" in a special 35MM screening. The film, a science fiction, comedy, drama, and mystery from 2006, runs for 100 minutes. The screening on September 16th will include an introduction by Alex Lei. This event is part of the "2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die" series.

event_title: Werewolf in a Women’s Prison with Jeff Leroy (Director)
film_description: A woman wakes up in a corrupt prison after being attacked by a werewolf while camping with her boyfriend. She learns that her boyfriend was torn apart, and she is the only suspect.
event_description: Experience 'Werewolf in a Women’s Prison,' a film by action-horror maverick Jeff Leroy. This screening is followed by a Q&A session with director Jeff Leroy and special guests. The film, released in 2006, is an homage to 1970s exploitation, blending old-school werewolf tropes with the women-in-prison formula, delivering a gleefully relentless and over-the-top stew of monsters, practical gore, and sexy sleaze.

event_title: Gorilla Gorilla with Filmmakers
film_description: After her divisive debut, filmmaker Anne embarks on her sophomore effort, 'In Memory of Anne Heche.' The production quickly deteriorates as scenes go wrong, actors depart, and Anne's difficult relationship with her lead actress sours, taking a turn for the worse.
event_description: The event features a screening of the film 'Gorilla Gorilla'. Doors open at 7:00 PM, with the film beginning at 8:00 PM. Following the screening, there will be a Q&A session with the filmmakers starting at 9:45 PM.

event_title: The Wild Palms: Made in U.S.A & 2 or 3 Things I Know About Her with Michael Witt (Professor and Author)
film_title: The Wild Palms: Made in U.S.A & 2 or 3 Things I Know About Her
film_description: This screening presents a unique Godardian concept: a 35mm projection of both "Made in U.S.A." and "2 or 3 Things I Know About Her" as a single, intertwined work. The innovative presentation draws inspiration from William Faulkner’s novel "The Wild Palms," which similarly combines two distinct narrative strands.
event_description: This special 35mm performance features Jean-Luc Godard's "Made in U.S.A." (1966, 85 min) and "2 or 3 Things I Know About Her" (1967, 87 min), presented as a single, integrated work. The screening is introduced by Michael Witt, a professor and author, who will delve into Godard's radical proposition inspired by William Faulkner's "The Wild Palms." The films' reels and narratives are intertwined, reflecting Faulkner's experimental structure, which significantly influenced French cinema and Godard's own practice of juxtaposing self-contained blocks and film reels.

event_title: Leonora in the Morning Light with Thor Klein (Filmmaker), Lena Vurma (Filmmaker), Pam Grossman (Moderator)
film_description: Leonora Carrington, an outstanding figure of surrealism, along with Frida Kahlo, was one of Mexico's most famous painters. As the long-time partner of Max Ernst and close friend of André Breton and Jean Miró, she continually struggles with her visionary imagination, which often triggers serious psychological crises.
event_presenters: Thor Klein (Filmmaker), Lena Vurma (Filmmaker), Pam Grossman (Moderator)
event_description: This screening of "Leonora in the Morning Light" will be followed by a Q&A session with filmmakers Thor Klein and Lena Vurma, moderated by Pam Grossman. The film, set in the 1930s, explores the life of painter Leonora Carrington, her involvement with the surrealist movement, and her journey of self-empowerment.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Thor Klein (Filmmaker), Lena Vurma (Filmmaker), Pam Grossman (Moderator)

event_title: Rapt with Liberté et Patrie with Michael Witt (Professor and Author)
film_description: A double feature that showcases the profound influence of Swiss author Charles-Ferdinand Ramuz on filmmaking, a recurrent reference throughout Godard's career. The program brings together Dimitri Kirsanoff’s early sound film, the dark Alpine revenge melodrama "Rapt," and Jean-Luc Godard and Anne-Marie Miéville’s autobiographical video essay "Liberté et Patrie," inspired by Ramuz's novel "Aimé Pache, peintre vaudois."
event_description: This event features a double screening of Dimitri Kirsanoff's 1934 film "Rapt" and Jean-Luc Godard and Anne-Marie Miéville's 2002 film "Liberté et Patrie." The films are presented within the "Literary Adaptation II: Charles-Ferdinand Ramuz" series, highlighting Ramuz's literary impact on Godard and other filmmakers. The 7 PM screening includes an introduction and a post-screening conversation with Michael Witt, a professor and author.

event_title: Paper Tiger with James Gray and members of the cast and crew
film_description: Two brothers who pursue a lucrative business opportunity in 1980's Queens, find themselves caught up in a scheme involving the Russian mafia.
event_presenters: James Gray and members of the cast and crew
event_description: Film at Lincoln Center announces James Gray's Paper Tiger as the Opening Night selection of the 64th New York Film Festival. The film will make its North American premiere in a gala debut at Alice Tully Hall, with Gray and members of the cast and crew in attendance. This marks Gray’s fourth film to be selected for the New York Film Festival.

screenings.in_person_appearence: James Gray and members of the cast and crew

event_title: Joy of Joys with Jonathan Glazer (Director)
film_description: This documentary goes behind the scenes at Abbey Road Studios to capture the recording of the Mercury Prize–nominated HELP(2), a 2026 charity album from War Child Records, which aids children in conflict zones around the world. To make the film, Glazer enlisted some crucial help: young schoolkids from London were equipped with their own digital cameras and encouraged to shoot the studio recordings any way they wanted. Their curiosity and creativity are paralleled in footage taken by high-spirited children in war-torn parts of the globe—Gaza, Sudan, Ukraine, Yemen—whom Glazer also supplied with cameras. The resulting film, which Glazer and regular music collaborator Mica Levi have dubbed “by children, for children,” serves as a testament to youthful openness and wonder amidst the evils of the adult world.
event_description: The film "Joy of Joys" will have its world premiere as part of the 64th New York Film Festival. Following the screening, there will be an extended Q&A session with director Jonathan Glazer.

event_title: Godzilla Minus Zero with Takashi Yamazaki (Director) and members of the cast and crew
film_description: War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.
event_presenters: Takashi Yamazaki (Director) and members of the cast and crew
event_description: The world premiere of Takashi Yamazaki’s "Godzilla Minus Zero" will be presented as the Spotlight Gala selection for the 64th New York Film Festival. Director Yamazaki and members of the cast and crew will be in attendance for the premiere presentation. The film is a follow-up to the triumphant "Godzilla Minus One," further exploring the timeless franchise with innovative craft and human drama.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Takashi Yamazaki (Director) and members of the cast and crew

event_title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed with Order of the Illusive (Live Accompaniment)
film_description: Taken from The Arabian Nights, a wicked sorcerer and the beautiful prince Achmed battle one against the other during a series of wondrous adventures.
event_description: Experience the centennial of "The Adventures of Prince Achmed," the world's oldest animated feature film, with a live, original accompaniment by Order of the Illusive. The performance features Bradford Reed on the pencilina, an instrument of his own design, and drums, alongside Zach Layton on 17-string bass and effects. This unique presentation blends experimental and ambient rock to bring the silent film experience to contemporary audiences.

event_title: The Scout with Paula González-Nasser (Filmmaker)
film_description: Sofia is a location scout for a TV show in New York City. Over the course of one day, she is invited into homes, businesses, and lives across the city, witnessing the private spaces and dramas of countless strangers, until her work takes a sudden, personal turn.
event_description: This screening of Paula González-Nasser's film, "The Scout", will be followed by a post-screening conversation with the filmmaker. The film delves into the quiet journey of a location scout through other people's worlds as she seeks her own.

event_title: Idlewild with Jayson Buford
film_description: A reticent piano player Percival, along with Rooster, his flamboyant lead performer and manager, struggle to keep their speakeasy, in the Prohibition-era South, out of the hands of gangsters who want to take it over.
event_description: Idlewild screens as part of “2006 Movies You Must See Before You Die,” curated by Steve Macfarlane, and will include an introduction by Jayson Buford.

event_title: Moi, un noir with J. Hoberman (Critic)
film_description: Winner of the prestigious Prix Louis Delluc in 1958, "Moi, un noir" marked Jean Rouch's break with traditional ethnography, and his embrace of the collaborative and improvisatory strategies he called "shared ethnography" and "ethnofiction". The film depicts an ordinary week in the lives of men and women from Niger who have migrated to Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire for work.
event_description: J. Hoberman will introduce Jean Rouch’s seminal film, "Moi, un noir," and sign copies of his brand-new anthology, "Across the Movi-Verse: Writing on Film, 2011–2021." This event celebrates the publication of Hoberman’s collection, which includes essays on various film topics, including an essay on "Moi, un noir."

event_title: Je Tu Il Elle with Introduction by Beatrice Loayza
film_description: Chantal Akerman’s boldly minimalistic first feature stars the writer-director herself as a young woman emerging from an existence of isolation, exploring themes of voyeurism and lesbian identity in a landmark depiction of sexuality in cinema.

event_title: Mario with Ken Auletta, Madeline Cuomo, Teddy Kunhardt
film_description: This moving new documentary explores the life and legacy of former New York Governor Mario Cuomo. Directed by the Emmy Award-winning team of George, Peter, and Teddy Kunhardt, the film traces Cuomo's journey from the son of Italian immigrants to a governor who championed government as a force for compassion. It features archival footage, family reflections, and excerpts from personal diaries.
event_presenters: Ken Auletta, Madeline Cuomo, Teddy Kunhardt
event_description: Join us for a screening of 'Mario,' a new documentary about former New York Governor Mario Cuomo. Following the screening, there will be a conversation with journalist Ken Auletta, Madeline Cuomo, and filmmaker Teddy Kunhardt. They will discuss the man behind the public figure, the ideals that animated his leadership, and his lasting influence on New York.

screenings.in_person_appearence: Ken Auletta, Madeline Cuomo, Teddy Kunhardt

event_title: Local Filmmaker Showcase: Shorts with Filmmakers
film_description: This showcase features a collection of short films from various filmmakers. The selected shorts include diverse narratives, from social commentary to personal reflection, offering a glimpse into contemporary independent cinema.
event_description: Experience an evening of diverse short films from local filmmakers, including "Mashed Potatoes" by Suha Araj, "Our Wonderful Future" by Jonah Aaron Goldstein, "Adidas Owns the Reality" by Keil Orion Troisi & Igor Vamos, "Grandma & Isabella" by Hannah Engelson, and "The Waves Within Us" by Muhammad Ali Haider. This is a free screening, and filmmakers will be present in-person. The event is part of the Local Filmmaker Showcase 2025 and supported by the Rockaway Film Festival.

event_title: Failed State with Filmmakers
film_description: Dale spends the majority of his time transporting various goods to people while attempting to carve out a social life in-between. Eventually the weight of work, his declining health, pressure from his manager and decaying social relations become too heavy to bear.
event_description: This free screening of "Failed State," by Christopher Jason Bell and Mitch Blummer, offers a docufictional look at a streetwise courier's struggles in New York City. The film, anchored by a captivating performance from Dale Smith, is a poignant portrayal of precarious living in America. Filmmakers will be present in-person for the event.

event_title: Symposium of Sorts: Radical Inquiries with the UNDO Fellows with Travis Wilkerson
film_title: Symposium of Sorts: Radical Inquiries with the UNDO Fellows
film_description: UnionDocs has brought together leading documentary artists and filmmakers with adventurous writers and critics for its third iteration of The UNDO Fellowship. This program aims to expand radical filmmaking practices and research new languages of documentary cinema, offering a platform for writers to delve into a filmmaker’s work.
event_description: This two-day convening upstate, held in partnership with the Experimental Media and Performing Arts Center (EMPAC) in Troy, NY, celebrates a year of research, writing, and filmmaking from the UNDO Fellowship. The symposium brings together artists, writers, and curious minds to explore the evolving landscape of documentary art through screenings, conversations, and engagement with works-in-progress.
